mitigation_descriptions: The sudoers file should be strictly edited such that passwords are always required and that users can’t spawn risky processes as users with higher privilege. By requiring a password, even if an adversary can get terminal access, they must know the password to run anything in the sudoers file.

Setting the timestamp_timeout to 0 will require the user to input their password every time sudo is executed. Similarly, ensuring that the tty_tickets setting is enabled will prevent this leakage across tty sessions.
Prevent adversary access to privileged accounts or access necessary to perform this technique. Consider removing and replacing system components suspected of being compromised.
reasoning: An unauthorized privilege escalation occurred on intranet-server where a user pivoted from www-data to jwilkinson and executed sudo commands as root to inspect sensitive files and firewall configurations.
remediation_plan: 1. Isolate the affected host intranet-server (172.26.243.167) from the network to stop ongoing adversary actions. 2. Terminate all active sessions associated with the www-data and jwilkinson accounts. 3. Audit and strictly configure the /etc/sudoers file to ensure password requirements are enforced and users cannot spawn unauthorized privileged processes. 4. Configure timestamp_timeout to 0 and enable tty_tickets to prevent sudo credential caching and leakage across sessions. 5. Invalidate compromised credentials and inspect the system for persistence or further unauthorized modifications.
